findings.title: PR comment template helpers are added to the wrong class
findings.body: The new `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` and `get_environment_info` helpers are added to `CommitContextIntegration`, but `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow` call them on `self` and extend `PRCommentWorkflow`, not `CommitContextIntegration`. `PRCommentWorkflow` has neither method, and this line also calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`, which does not exist because `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`. Generating or updating a suspect-PR comment will raise `AttributeError` instead of posting the comment.

findings.title: Feature flag replaces table data with hard-coded empty table
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, this branch passes `columns={[]}` and an empty `tableData` object to `TableWidgetVisualization` instead of the `fields`, `result.data`, and `result.meta` already computed above. Every dashboard table widget will render as an empty grid under the flag, and the existing loading, metadata, and custom field renderer behavior is lost. It should pass the same table data/columns that the legacy `StyledSimpleTableChart` path uses.

findings.title: Age/timestamp mutual exclusion is bypassed when either value is zero
findings.body: The validators use truthiness (`if self.initial_data.get("age")` and similarly for `timestamp`) to detect the other field. A report containing `age=0` plus `timestamp`, or `timestamp=0` plus `age`, passes validation even though the two fields are supposed to be mutually exclusive. `age=0` is a legitimate value for a fresh report. Use key presence such as `"age" in self.initial_data` and validate exactly one of the spec fields.

findings.title: Attribute key query cache key omits organization slug
findings.body: The React Query key is only `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, while `getTraceItemAttributeKeys` fetches `/organizations/${organization.slug}/trace-items/attributes/`. If the active organization changes while the query options hash to the same value (especially with no selected projects), React Query can serve attribute keys cached from the previous organization. Include `organization.slug` in the query key/options.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only filtered during search
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` is applied only after the `searchQuery.trim()` early return. With no search text, the function returns all `sorted` attributes, so `is_segment`, `project_id`, and `received` remain visible in the default attributes tree; they disappear only when the user searches. Apply the hidden-attribute filter unconditionally before the early return if these attributes are meant to be hidden.

findings.title: Custom cell renderers returning falsy ReactNodes are treated as absent
findings.body: The documented contract says the fallback runs when a custom renderer returns `undefined`, but the code checks `if (cell)` (and `renderDefaultHeadCell` does the same). Valid `ReactNode` return values such as `0`, `''`, `false`, or `null` are treated as no override and replaced by the default renderer, so a custom renderer cannot intentionally render an empty or zero-valued cell. Check `cell !== undefined` instead.
